summary: York County, Maine tower first built 1918; steel removed December 2025 as unsafe; a steering committee is weighing what comes next.

facts.design: 24-foot steel tower (1918); 47-foot steel tower (1934); 65-foot tower with catwalk (register, from 1981)
facts.status_note: The cab was removed in 2019 and the steel tower was removed in December 2025 because it was no longer safe. A steering committee has been formed to explore what comes next.

staffing.status: Watchman in 1920; Edward Cahoon named for 1963; register (1994) says the Town of York Fire Department staffed it

events.note: 24-foot steel tower erected in cooperation with the U.S. Forest Service (1918 annual report, quoted by Forest Lookouts); register also says built 1918
Watchman on duty late April to end of September; 36 fires reported by the watchman
Original tower extended to 40 feet and moved to Bear Mountain, Hartford; new 47-foot steel tower erected on the summit
July 23, 1950 fire believed caused by blueberry pickers, spotted by the lookout and spread through dry brush
Edward Cahoon of North Berwick named to man the tower this season
April 17, 1974 woods fire along a power line in the High Pine section, discovered by the tower
Register says the 47-foot tower was replaced by a 65-foot tower in 1981
New cab airlifted to the tower (Maine Historical Society photo inventory, quoted by Forest Lookouts)
Catwalk added (register); the register's Built field also gives 1985
Registered August 22, 1994; described as active and staffed by the Town of York Fire Department
Project to restore the tower began in 2014
Cab removed because it was in very poor shape
Steel removed in December 2025 because the footings and steel had deteriorated and were no longer safe

corrections.why: 14.3 m is the 47-foot tower of 1934. The register says that tower was replaced by a 65-foot tower in 1981 (19.8 m), which it calls the current tower. Human review advised: the 1994 register is the only source for the 65-foot height.

1985 is the register's Built field, but the register's own description and the Forest Lookouts annual-report excerpt date the first tower on the mountain to 1918. 1985 is the year the catwalk was added to the 1981 tower.

corrections.current: The rotted cab was taken off the 1940s steel tower, which still stands without a cab.
corrections.proposed: Cab removed in 2019 because it was in very poor shape; the steel itself was removed in December 2025.
corrections.why: The 2025 report says the cab came off in 2019 and the steel was removed in December 2025. No source read gives a 1940s date for this tower; the sources date the steel tower to 1934 (47 feet) or 1981 (65 feet).

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register Built field says 1985; the register description says a 65-foot tower replaced the 47-foot tower in 1981 with a catwalk in 1985; Forest Lookouts dates the first steel tower to 1918. Story uses 1918 for the first tower and reports the 1981 and 1985 dates as the register gives them.

Register says a 65-foot tower replaced the 47-foot tower in 1981; Forest Lookouts quotes a photo inventory describing only a new cab airlifted in 1981. Story reports both without deciding which is the full account.

notes_for_editor: Brief events not verified and left out of the record: 2007 winter repair, 2015 FFLA grant ($500), 2016 closure, 2018 engineering assessment, 2019 closure to the public. None of those pages were read in this pass; treat them as unconfirmed. The 1981 and 1985 dates conflict between the register and the Forest Lookouts excerpt. The 2025 report does not say whether the footings were removed, so the story says nothing about remains beyond what sources state. Photos: none added; the Forest Lookouts page has none with a stated license. The register's '24 fire tower' wording is read as a 24-foot tower, matching the 1918 annual-report quote.
